editorial.headline: Event Catering: Contract Food Service, Delivered to the Occasion
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers contracted, ready-to-eat food service for specified events—nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Event catering is the business of preparing and supplying food under a contract with a client, at a location chosen by that client, for a particular occasion. Its centre of gravity is the event itself: an office gathering, celebration, party, seminar, meeting, or a comparable occasion. The food is ready to consume, commonly delivered to the workplace or event venue, and the service can extend beyond delivery to include waitstaff serving guests or participants while the occasion is under way.

That definition matters because the activity is structured around an agreed event engagement rather than an undifferentiated food operation. The client identifies the occasion and location; the operator prepares and provides the food accordingly. In practical terms, the work joins preparation, delivery and, where required, on-site service into one contracted offering. It is a category for businesses whose commercial proposition is feeding a defined gathering with food ready for guests, rather than merely producing food for onward sale.

The registration field is broad. The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, so the record does not confine it to one end of the business spectrum. At the national level, its PMA status is TERBUKA and foreign ownership may reach 100%. That is the straightforward national position: foreign ownership is permitted up to full ownership for this activity.

Bali does not reverse that position. The provincial rule blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, island-wide and permanently, but this activity is recorded as not blocked by that moratorium. At Besar scale, the OSS risk position is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which is why the record places it outside the moratorium block. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: the activity remains available for PMA registration in Bali, while the record specifically signals its higher-risk treatment at the Besar end of the scale range. For a founder, that distinction is the essential one—national openness is real here, and Bali does not impose the moratorium barrier on this activity.
